title: Adaptive Envelope Throttler and Contract Reconciliation for Console Events
creator: Ava Park
description: Implement a lightweight, policy-driven Envelope Throttler combined with an in-path Contract Reconciliation step for Console usage events. The goal is to reduce tail latency and error spikes during bursts by applying tenant-aware throttling and lightweight transformations (coercions, field mapping, and safe-drop) to bring malformed or evolved events into compliance rather than rejecting them outright. This feature sits in the intake plane before the canonicalizer and complements existing schema guards by providing graceful degradation, transparent metrics, and debug hooks for downstream debugging.
design_notes: Throttler responsibilities: per-tenant token-bucket with dynamic capacity based on recent success rate, global emergency limiter, and adaptive slow-start for cold tenants.

Contract Reconciliation: configurable transformation pipeline (rename/migrate fields, coerce types, remove optional noisy fields) + retention of original payload for audit when transformations were applied.
Failure semantics: soft-fail path persists original event to a quarantine S3-like store and emits a structured rejection event; hard quota breaches return 429 with backoff hints.
Placement: run as an ingress sidecar in the Console intake cluster and as a stand-alone stateless service for Dedicated deployments behind the existing load balancer.
Policy configuration: YAML policy per-tenant with defaults, versioned in Config Service; include a sim-mode (dry-run) that reports but does not apply transformations for 48h before flip.

Observability: emit per-event reason tags, transformation diffs (summary only), throttling_decision and quota_remaining metrics. Trace ID propagation required for linkability to downstream processing.
Privacy: when persisting transformed/original payloads to quarantine, strip PII fields as per compliance policy; integrate with KMS for encryption-at-rest.
Performance: aim for <1ms median added latency and <5ms p95 when not interacting with quarantine store. Use local memory caches for policy and metrics to avoid blocking RPCs.
Compatibility: fallback to existing canonicalizer if contract reconciliation is disabled; ensure feature gate for runtime rollout.
Edge cases: large events (over 1MB) should be fast-failed to avoid amplification; provide guidance on client-side sampling and batching improvements.
Docs & SDK: include sample policy templates and SDK helpers to create compatible envelopes from clients.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress cluster serves throttled/rewritten events and passes existing canonicalizer tests for 99% of live telemetry traffic in dry-run mode.
In active mode, system reduces console-frontend 5xx spikes by >=40% in synthetic burst test and reduces downstream rejection rate by >=60% in replay tests.
Metrics: throttling_decision and reconciliation_count are present in Grafana dashboards; traces link to reconciliation decisions in Zipkin/Jaeger.
Performance: additional median latency <1ms, p95 <5ms for the reconciliation path when the quarantine store is healthy.
Security: quarantine payloads are encrypted and access-controlled; design passes security review checklist and threat model signoff.
Rollout: canary targets 5% of tenants with sim-mode enabled, then 20%, then global with automated rollback on increased error-rate signal.
Documentation: runbook for on-call describing how to interpret throttling signals and how to flip tenant policy flags.
Automated tests: unit tests for policy parser, e2e replay harness for transformation rules and stress tests for burst behavior.
PRs merged and an integration job added to CI that validates policy compatibility against the canonical schema.
No data loss in normal operating envelopes and quarantined items retained according to retention policy.
Feature gate 'adaptive_envelope_throttler' exists and respects per-tenant override.
rollout_plan: Week 0: merge design doc and proto API; Security review & KMS integration plan (dry-run).
Week 1: implement policy engine + unit tests; create sim-mode and telemetry hooks.
Week 2: sidecar + standalone service implementation; add quarantine writer and basic dashboard panels.
Week 3: internal dry-run for 48h on canary tenants; collect metrics and iterate rules to reduce false positives.
Week 4: phased canary rollout (5% -> 20% -> 50%) with automated rollback thresholds for error-rate and latency.
Week 5: global flip, monitor for 72h; retro and postmortem if regressions observed.
Post-release: runbook updates, SDK policy templates, and a 90-day retention clean-up job for quarantine.
Backout: disable feature gate and revert policy assignment; run retrospective to tune heuristics.
Owner for rollout: Rafael Gomez; SRE on-call: Priya Nair.
Communication: announce to Console users + Support with guidance and opt-out window for enterprise customers.
Telemetry: create dashboard 'Adaptive Envelope Throttler' and add alert thresholds to PagerDuty.
Contingency: if quarantine store shows >0.5% write errors, automatically scale back to sim-mode and notify on-call.
Demo: record short demo video for Developer Docs showing sim-mode reports and how to author a tenant policy.
Post-launch audit: sample 100 reconciled events per week per major tenant and validate correctness.
Metrics to validate rollback: 5xx rate, reconciliation_count, quarantine_write_errors, p95_latency.
Compliance: provide audit log entries to Compliance team for tenant policy changes.
QA checklist: fuzz tests for schema permutations; replay historic 7-day window to validate behavior.
Estimate: 8 points, cross-functional scope requires 2 SRE days for instrumentation and capacity tuning.
Release milestone: console-2026.03 target.
Security review tracked in PR: https://confluence.redwood.ai/security/reviews/AEThrottler-2026
risks: False positives in reconciliation could hide legitimate data schema regressions; mitigated by sim-mode and sample audits.
Quarantine store could become a hotspot during large bursts; mitigation: write batching, async buffering, and backoff.
Policy misconfiguration risk — add validation and preview tooling in Console before enabling policies.
Performance regressions in low-memory environments; provide a lightweight config that disables local caching.
Encryption/KMS integration adds latency for quarantine writes; use envelope-level caching of DEKs.
Customer trust: altering payload content requires clear communication and audit trails to avoid operational surprises.
Complexity of rollout across Hosted/Dedicated/Private — ensure the feature gate and deployment topology are validated in staging.
Potential interaction with rate limiter upstream causing double-throttling; coordinate signals with Rate Limiting team.
Operational burden of new dashboards and alerts; commit to rotating alert owner and trimming noisey signals post-canary.
Legal/regulatory: quarantining user data requires retention policy and deletion hooks; coordinate with Legal & Compliance.
